dossier.purpose: systemd is the Linux system and service manager (PID 1 in system mode, one instance per user session in user mode; README.md:3, docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:169-172) plus a suite of daemons and tools (journald, udev, logind, networkd, resolved, nspawn, ...). The README makes no workflow-engine claims; the facts relevant to a scheduling/supervision need come from the man pages and code. (1) Scheduling: .timer units with OnCalendar= and monotonic On*Sec= triggers, Persistent= catch-up via on-disk stamp files, RandomizedDelaySec=, DeferReactivation= (man/systemd.timer.xml:107-441); a timer enqueues a start job on its service (src/core/timer.c:668); systemd-run can create transient timer+service pairs for arbitrary commands (man/systemd-run.xml:64-89,453-506); transient units are kept under /run/systemd/transient (man/systemd.unit.xml:403-404). Shipped timers: systemd-tmpfiles-clean.timer and the sysupdate timers (units/*.timer). (2) DAG: the unit dependency graph (Requires=/Wants=/BindsTo=, After=/Before=, OnSuccess=/OnFailure=) is resolved into an in-memory job transaction when a unit is started; ordering cycles are broken by deleting jobs (src/core/transaction.c:425-511); no persisted per-run DAG instance was found. (3) Retries: Restart= with RestartSec=/RestartSteps=/RestartMaxDelaySec=/RestartRandomizedDelaySec= (new in v262), limited by StartLimitIntervalSec=/StartLimitBurst= (default 5 starts per 10 s, src/basic/constants.h:20-21); Restart=always/on-success are rejected for Type=oneshot (src/core/service.c:1059-1060). (4) Process-tree bounds: every unit gets a cgroup; KillMode=control-group is the default (src/core/kill.h:8); stop sends SIGTERM then SIGKILL after TimeoutStopSec= (man/systemd.kill.xml:63-101); TasksMax= (default 15% of pid limits, man/systemd-system.conf.xml:225-234), MemoryMax=, slice ConcurrencySoftMax=/ConcurrencyHardMax=/ActivatingConcurrencyMax=; RuntimeMaxSec= is ignored for Type=oneshot (src/core/service.c:1077-1078). (5) History: journald entries carry a per-run INVOCATION_ID (man/systemd.exec.xml:4245-4251; journalctl -I/--invocation, man/journalctl.xml:354-376) and job results are logged with JOB_ID/JOB_RESULT (src/core/job.c:802-831); successfully finished units are unloaded immediately while failed ones stay in memory until reset-failed unless --collect/CollectMode=inactive-or-failed is used (man/systemd-run.xml:545-553); systemctl list-timers shows only the last trigger (man/systemctl.xml:197-200). (6) UI: CLI only (systemctl, systemd-run, journalctl, systemd-analyze); the only web page in the repo is the journal viewer at /browse of systemd-journal-gatewayd (man/systemd-journal-gatewayd.service.xml:165-168). (7) Cancellation: systemctl stop/kill act on running units; systemctl cancel/CancelJob only remove queued jobs (man/systemctl.xml:1377-1382; man/org.freedesktop.systemd1.xml:1498-1501). No rollback or compensation mechanism for side effects was found; ExecStopPost= is the documented cleanup hook (man/systemd.service.xml:594-598).

claims.claim: Project self-description: 'System and Service Manager'; most documentation is on systemd.io; a Code Map (docs/ARCHITECTURE.md) and a hacking guide are linked.
Build requirements are kept in the plain-text README file and release changes in NEWS.
Stable branches with backported patches are available in the separate systemd-stable repository.
A security bug bounty program (sponsored by the Sovereign Tech Fund, hosted on YesWeHack) exists; this is an external program and not verifiable from the repository.
Distribution packages built from git main, and from the latest stable release, are available as OBS repositories.
Badges advertise Semaphore CI, Coverity, OSS-Fuzz, CIFuzz, CII Best Practices, Coveralls coverage and OpenSSF Scorecard.
License: 'LGPL-2.1-or-later for all code, exceptions noted in LICENSES/README.md'.

Kernels below 5.10 ('minimum baseline') are 'not supported at all'; below 5.14 ('recommended baseline') have significant gaps and get taint flag 'old-kernel'; newer kernel APIs fall back gracefully when unavailable.
The build prefix must be /usr/; split-usr and unmerged-usr systems are no longer supported.
Policy: main and latest releases should compile on current popular distributions; regularly tested on amd64, i386, arm64, ppc64el and s390x.
Default shared linking is recommended; mixing versions of components that are normally built together is not tested upstream and is not supported.

A fully static 'systemd' binary usable as PID 1 in a container can be built with --default-library=static --prefer-static -Dbuild-static=true -Dsystemd-multicall-binary=true; it does not use dlopen() or NSS.
Toolchain/runtime requirements: glibc >= 2.34 or musl >= 1.2.6, python >= 3.9, meson >= 0.62.0, ninja, gcc >= 8.4; dbus >= 1.4.0 is 'strictly speaking optional, but recommended'.

Taint flags: the manager warns on missing cgroup support ('cgroups-missing'), the old cgroup hierarchy ('cgroupsv1'), a local-time hardware clock, a bad /var/run, UID/GID range problems; readable via busctl get-property ... Tainted.

install.method: Build from source with Meson/Ninja, then install
install.command: meson setup build/ && ninja -C build/ ; sudo meson install -C build/ --no-rebuild   (or: DESTDIR=... meson install -C build/)

install.method: Distribution packages from SUSE OBS repositories (project system:systemd for git main, system:systemd:stable for the latest release)
install.command: Follow the per-distribution repository instructions at https://software.opensuse.org//download.html?project=system%3Asystemd&package=systemd (linked page not opened; no package-manager command is given in the repo). For Secure Boot, docs/HACKING.md also shows: wget https://build.opensuse.org/projects/system:systemd/signing_keys/download?kind=ssl -O- | openssl x509 -inform pem -outform der -out obs.der ; run0 mokutil --import obs.der

install.method: Build distribution packages with mkosi, then upgrade the host with the distro package manager
install.command: mkosi -d <distribution> -r <release> -t none -f ; run0 dnf upgrade build/mkosi.builddir/<distribution>~<release>~<architecture>/*.rpm   (Debian/Ubuntu: run0 apt-get install .../*.deb; Arch: run0 pacman --upgrade --needed --noconfirm .../*.pkg.tar; openSUSE: run0 zypper --non-interactive install --allow-unsigned-rpm .../*.rpm)

install.method: Build and boot a throwaway OS image containing the built systemd (nspawn or qemu) instead of installing on the host
install.command: mkosi -f genkey ; mkosi -f box -- meson setup -Dbpf-framework=disabled build ; mkosi -f box -- meson compile -C build ; mkosi -f box -- meson compile -C build mkosi ; mkosi boot   (or: mkosi vm)

install.method: Create a source tarball from a git tag (documented example uses v250)

platforms.linux_x86_64: yes - amd64 is listed as a regularly tested architecture (README:333-336) and unit tests run on x86_64 ubuntu-24.04 runners (.github/workflows/unit-tests.yml:24-27). Requires Linux >= 5.10 (>= 5.14 recommended; README:58-68), cgroup v2 (src/core/main.c:3807-3822), glibc >= 2.34 or musl >= 1.2.6 (README:213-214) and a merged /usr (README:311-316).
platforms.wsl2: unknown - no WSL install or support statement in README.md, README, docs/*.md or .github/; upstream only detects WSL as a container-like virtualization type (src/basic/virt.c:659-665; man/systemd-detect-virt.xml:192-193,214-219; ConditionVirtualization=wsl at man/systemd.unit.xml:1451).
platforms.macos_arm64: no - 'systemd is not portable to non-Linux systems' and portability patches are not accepted (docs/PORTABILITY_AND_STABILITY.md:111-113); no macOS install method is documented. (Linux arm64 is a different target: arm64 is a regularly tested architecture, README:333-336, .github/workflows/unit-tests.yml:29-32.)
platforms.gpu: no - nothing in README.md, README or docs requires or uses a GPU; the only GPU-adjacent mention is the udev 'render' and 'video' group names (README:406-407).

integrations.cli: yes - systemctl (src/systemctl/meson.build:43-56; verbs list-timers, list-jobs, cancel, kill, clean, freeze at src/systemctl/systemctl.c:922,957-963,1022-1024), systemd-run and its run0 symlink (src/run/meson.build:3-13; transient timers via --on-calendar/--on-active etc., man/systemd-run.xml:453-506; --wait propagates the unit result as exit status, src/run/run.c:2491-2502), journalctl (src/journal/journalctl.c:1139; -I/--invocation, man/journalctl.xml:354-376), systemd-analyze (calendar, verify, dot, plot; src/analyze/analyze.c:216-273), loginctl enable-linger (man/loginctl.xml:186-195). The CLI is declared stable but its human-readable output generally is not (docs/PORTABILITY_AND_STABILITY.md:42-49).
integrations.mcp: none found - searches for 'MCP' / 'Model Context Protocol' across src/, man/, docs/, tools/, mkosi/, .github/, README*, NEWS and AGENTS.md returned no matches.
integrations.sdk_or_api: yes - D-Bus API org.freedesktop.systemd1 (man/org.freedesktop.systemd1.xml; e.g. CancelJob at src/core/dbus-manager.c:3310); Varlink API io.systemd.Manager / io.systemd.Unit / io.systemd.Job incl. StartTransient (src/core/varlink.c:430-444; socket /run/systemd/io.systemd.Manager at line 554; NEWS:191-196); C libraries libsystemd (sd-bus, sd-event, sd-journal, sd-varlink, ...; README:340-346; docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:31-32); the sd_notify socket protocol. D-Bus, Varlink, libsystemd's public interface and the unit-file format are declared stable (docs/PORTABILITY_AND_STABILITY.md:30-56). No HTTP/REST API for the manager; HTTP exists only in systemd-journal-gatewayd for journal data (man/systemd-journal-gatewayd.service.xml:38-42).
integrations.claude_code_or_codex: none found as a user-facing integration. Repo-internal only: .github/workflows/claude-review.yml (CI job that gives maintainers a Claude Code PR review via '@claude'; header lines 1-4; installs a pinned, SHA-256-checked Claude Code binary at lines 276-291 and authenticates to AWS Bedrock via OIDC at lines 293-297), AGENTS.md (guidance file for AI coding agents contributing to this repository), and the LLM/AI contribution policy in docs/CONTRIBUTING.md:53-69.

readme.telemetry_and_network: No telemetry found: case-insensitive searches of src/, man/, docs/, NEWS and README* for 'telemetry', 'phone home' and 'usage statistics' returned no matches. No account or registration concept found; PID 1 inputs are local (unit files, credentials, kernel command line, D-Bus; docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:169-170); some daemons need local OS users/groups (README:401-426). Network use is confined to optional components that act only when built, enabled or invoked: systemd-timesyncd (NTP; NTP= empty by default with a compiled-in fallback list, man/timesyncd.conf.xml:55-74; build default time1-4.google.com, meson_options.txt:395-397), systemd-resolved (compiled-in default DNS server list 1.1.1.1 / 8.8.8.8 / 9.9.9.9 etc., meson_options.txt:392-394), systemd-networkd, systemd-journal-remote/upload/gatewayd (gatewayd listens on port 19531, plain HTTP unless --cert/--key, man/systemd-journal-gatewayd.service.xml:38-42), importctl/importd and systemd-sysupdate (download images/updates; man/importctl.xml:24, man/systemd-sysupdate.xml:31), systemd-imds (cloud IMDS at 169.254.169.254, src/imds/imdsd.c:68) and the experimental 'systemd-report upload' (HTTP(S) POST only when run with --url or when a socket exists under /run/systemd/report.upload/; plain http is unencrypted and --trust=all disables certificate checks; man/systemd-report.xml:36-37,85-97,134-143,170-174). The shipped systemd-report@.service runs systemd-report with no verb (units/systemd-report@.service.in:18) and no shipped timer calls it; the shipped timers are systemd-tmpfiles-clean.timer (system and user) and the two sysupdate timers (units/*.timer, units/user/systemd-tmpfiles-clean.timer). The upstream preset file enables systemd-networkd, systemd-resolved and systemd-timesyncd and disables journal-gatewayd/remote/upload (presets/90-systemd.preset:32-48,68-70); whether a distribution applies it was not checked.

languages: C (~1,849 .c files under src/; primary language)
Python (~66 .py files: build tooling, ukify, test harnesses)

entry_points.what: main() of the 'systemd' service manager (PID 1 system instance and --user instance); /sbin/init is a symlink to it (src/core/meson.build:337-340)
systemd-executor: deserializes the unit's exec context, applies sandboxing/cgroup/namespaces, then execve()s the command; spawned by PID 1 via posix_spawn (src/core/execute.c:580-588)
systemd-run (and run0 symlink): transient service/scope/timer/path/socket units for arbitrary commands; --wait returns the unit result as exit status (run.c:2491-2502)
systemd-journald daemon (structured logs incl. invocation-ID tagging)
journalctl CLI (-u, -I/--invocation, time filters, JSON output)
systemd-analyze (calendar, verify, dot, plot, critical-chain, security, ...)
Timer unit type (not an executable): timer_enter_waiting (372) computes next elapse; timer_enter_running (643) enqueues the start job

code.architecture: C code base built with Meson. Layering per docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:19-70: src/fundamental -> src/basic -> src/libsystemd (public libsystemd.so: sd-bus, sd-event, sd-journal, sd-varlink, sd-future fibers, ...) -> src/shared (private libsystemd-shared-<nnn>.so); every other src/ subdirectory is one component. Service manager = src/core: main.c (PID 1 / --user), manager.c, unit.c, unit types service.c, timer.c, path.c, socket.c, slice.c, scope.c, target.c, mount.c, device.c, swap.c, automount.c; job.c + transaction.c (job queue, merging, ordering-cycle breaking); cgroup.c + kill.c (and unit_kill_context in unit.c:5081-5179) bound and kill process trees; execute.c + executor.c/exec-invoke.c start each command through the separate systemd-executor binary via posix_spawn into the unit's cgroup (execute.c:525-608); dbus-*.c and varlink-*.c expose the D-Bus and Varlink APIs (varlink.c:430-444). Timers: timer.c computes the next elapse (calendar expressions parsed by src/shared/calendarspec.c, timer.c:451), enqueues JOB_START with JOB_REPLACE (timer.c:668) and stores the last trigger time in stamp files under /var/lib/systemd/timers or ~/.local/share/systemd/timers (timer.c:131-169,679-680). Logging/history: src/journal (journald, journalctl), src/libsystemd/sd-journal, src/journal-remote (gatewayd, remote, upload). Clients: src/systemctl, src/run (systemd-run/run0), src/analyze, src/cgls, src/cgtop, src/tmpfiles. Other daemons: src/udev, src/login, src/network, src/resolve, src/nspawn, src/home, src/machine, src/oom, ... Docs: man/*.xml (DocBook) and docs/*.md; tests in src/test, per-component test-*.c, src/fuzz and test/.
code.packaging_and_release: No project-built binary artifacts. Upstream releases are GPG-signed git tags (docs/RELEASE.md:21,43) plus a GitHub release that .github/workflows/make-release.yml creates as a draft on 'v*' tags using softprops/action-gh-release, with no files attached and the prerelease flag set for -rc tags (lines 5-9,22-26). No checksum, signature, SBOM or provenance/attestation step was found in any workflow (searching .github for gpg/cosign/attest/provenance/sha256sum/sigstore only hit apt LLVM key setup in build-test.sh:132-134 and a hash check of the downloaded Claude Code CLI in claude-review.yml:276-291). Source tarballs are documented via 'git archive' (README:298-299); meson.build has no dist script. Binary packages come from SUSE OBS (project system:systemd for main, system:systemd:stable for releases: .obs/workflows.yml:1-10; docs/RELEASE.md:16,29,34; README.md:41-42; systemd-boot there is signed with a self-signed OBS key, docs/HACKING.md:161-167), Fedora Copr/Packit (.packit.yml:29-48) and Debian/Ubuntu packaging on salsa.debian.org (docs/RELEASE.md:31-33). Version lives in meson.version (262; docs/RELEASE.md:17). Stable branches v<N>-stable live in this repo since v256, older ones in systemd/systemd-stable (docs/RELEASE.md:41). OpenSSF Scorecard runs weekly (.github/workflows/scorecards.yml:8-9,36-41).
code.tests_and_ci: Frameworks: Meson test runner (default suite excludes clang-tidy, coccinelle, unused-symbols and integration-tests: meson.build:16-21); C unit tests in 406 test-*.c files under src/ (264 in src/test/); 54 fuzz-*.c files (2 are helpers) replayed on corpora under test/fuzz/ (-Dfuzz-tests defaults true: meson_options.txt:539-540) and fuzzed continuously via OSS-Fuzz/CIFuzz/ClusterFuzzLite; 73 integration-test groups test/integration-tests/TEST-*/ with ~314 shell scripts test/units/TEST-*.sh run in mkosi-built nspawn/QEMU images (test/integration-tests/README.md:1-60; docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:127-134); ~66 Python files include harnesses (test/test-network, src/ukify/test, ...). Approximate total: ~770 test/fuzz source files. Scheduling/supervision-relevant tests: TEST-53-TIMER (RandomizedDelaySec-persistent/-reload, clock-change, restart-trigger), TEST-07-PID1 (DeferReactivation, concurrency, start-limit, subgroup-kill, transient), TEST-03-JOBS, TEST-16-EXTEND-TIMEOUT, TEST-18-FAILUREACTION, TEST-19-CGROUP, TEST-30-ONCLOCKCHANGE, TEST-38-FREEZER, TEST-04-JOURNAL.invocation, plus src/test/test-calendarspec.c and src/libsystemd/sd-event/test-event.c. CI workflows (.github/workflows): unit-tests.yml (PRs to main/stable; GCC, GCC+ASan/UBSan, Clang, Clang release, Clang+ASan/UBSan on x86_64, arm64, armhf cross, ppc64le, s390x, plus a musl/postmarketOS job; meson test with -Dtests=unsafe -Dslow-tests=true -Dfuzz-tests=true), build-test.yml (gcc 11/13, clang 14/16/18, riscv64/armhf cross, Python 3.9), mkosi.yml (build and boot images for arch, debian, ubuntu, fedora, opensuse, centos, postmarketos), linter.yml (super-linter/actionlint, mypy, ruff, clang-tidy, coccinelle, man-rules), cifuzz.yml (OSS-Fuzz CIFuzz, ASan/UBSan/MSan x86_64 and ASan i386, 600 s), cflite-pr.yml, coverage.yml (daily), coverity.yml (daily), scorecards.yml (weekly), differential-shellcheck.yml, claude-review.yml, labeler/issue-labeler/gather-pr-metadata/development-freeze. Outside GitHub: .semaphore/semaphore.yml (Debian autopkgtest in LXC), .packit.yml (Fedora Copr builds plus tests), .obs/workflows.yml (OBS CI builds).
code.dependencies: Root meson.build: 45 pkg-config dependency() lookups (libbpf, libmount, libseccomp, libselinux, libapparmor, libacl, audit, blkid, libkmod, pam, libcryptsetup, libcurl, libmicrohttpd, openssl, gnutls, tss2-*, libfido2, p11-kit, libdw/libelf, zlib, bzip2, liblzma, liblz4, libzstd, libarchive, xkbcommon, libpcre2-8, glib-2.0/gobject-2.0/gio-2.0, dbus-1, libcrypt, libidn2, libqrencode, libgcrypt, pwquality/passwdqc, xencontrol, fdisk, polkit-gobject-1, libucontext on musl only) plus find_library for m, pam and bz2 (meson.build:1026,1209,1370) and FuzzingEngine for fuzzer builds (meson.build:373); nearly all are gated by feature options (meson_options.txt). No dependency() calls exist in sub-directory meson.build files. Required build tooling per README:251-266: pkg-config, gperf, python >= 3.9 + jinja2, meson >= 0.62.0 (meson.build:13), ninja, gcc >= 8.4 or clang, binutils >= 2.35; required libs: glibc >= 2.34 or musl >= 1.2.6, libmount >= 2.30 (README:213-217; meson.build:1076-1078). .github/workflows/requirements.txt: 2 hash-pinned pip packages (meson==1.11.2, ninja==1.13.0). mkosi/**/mkosi.conf* (29 files) list distro packages for CI images. No Cargo.toml, go.mod, package.json or pyproject.toml found.
code.security_policy: docs/SECURITY.md (no root-level SECURITY.md): private disclosure via a GitHub Security Advisory (preferred) or systemd-security@redhat.com (docs/SECURITY.md:10-13); valid reports must reproduce on main with a real-world end-to-end reproducer that demonstrably violates a security boundary, and maintainers (mostly volunteers) give no fixed timeline (docs/SECURITY.md:22-29); a bug bounty is hosted on YesWeHack with Sovereign Tech Fund sponsorship (README.md:39).

claim_checks.claim: README.md:3 / docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:169-172 - systemd is the 'System and Service Manager': PID 1 in system mode and one instance per user session in user mode.
claim_checks.evidence: src/core/main.c:4028 main(); the runtime-scope switch handles the system boot path and the user manager (src/core/main.c:2617-2635); installed as the init symlink to lib/systemd/systemd (src/core/meson.build:337-340).

claim_checks.claim: docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:172-174 (linked from README.md:27) - each service process is started by posix_spawn()ing a separate systemd-executor binary with the serialized config passed via memfd.
claim_checks.evidence: src/core/execute.c:525-608 serializes the exec context to a memfd-backed file, posix_spawn_wrapper() runs 'systemd-executor --deserialize', the child is placed into the unit cgroup (CLONE_INTO_CGROUP or cg_attach, lines 600-605); src/core/meson.build:20-23,261-289 builds systemd-executor (or a multicall symlink).

claim_checks.claim: man/systemd.timer.xml:50-52 (documented behaviour, not README) - if the unit to activate is already active when a timer elapses it is not restarted and no new instance is spawned.
claim_checks.evidence: src/core/timer.c:668 queues JOB_START with JOB_REPLACE; src/core/unit.c:1957-1962 returns -EALREADY for active units and src/core/job.c:970-971 turns that into JOB_DONE; src/core/service.c:6388-6389 treats services still in condition/start-pre/start/start-post as not startable (no second run, no start-limit increment).

claim_checks.claim: README:58-59,65-68 - kernels below 5.10 are 'not supported at all'; below 5.14 is the 'recommended baseline' and sets taint 'old-kernel'.
claim_checks.evidence: Code differs: only a 5.14 constant exists (src/basic/constants.h:74-75, commented 'Recommended baseline'); older kernels just get a warning 'Your mileage may vary' and the 'old-kernel' taint (src/core/main.c:2619-2623; src/core/taint.c:62-65). A grep for "5.10" in src/ finds no check or refusal, so the 5.10 floor is documentation-only. By contrast cgroup v1 is refused outright (src/core/main.c:3807-3822).

claim_checks.claim: README:457-469 - the manager sets taint flags 'cgroups-missing' and 'cgroupsv1' (among others).
claim_checks.evidence: Code preferred over README: src/core/taint.c:35-83 sets only unmerged-usr, unmerged-bin, var-run-bad, local-hwclock, support-ended, old-kernel, overflowuid-not-65534, overflowgid-not-65534, short-uid-range, short-gid-range. 'cgroups-missing' appears only in README:463; 'cgroupsv1' only in README:464 and man/org.freedesktop.systemd1.xml:1855. PID 1 now refuses to run on cgroup v1 (src/core/main.c:3807-3822) and NEWS:2837-2839 (v258) records the removal.

claim_checks.claim: README:311-316 - the build prefix must be /usr/; split-usr and unmerged-usr systems are no longer supported.
claim_checks.evidence: meson.build:8 only sets prefix=/usr as a default and errors only when the prefix is not absolute (meson.build:123-126); at runtime unmerged layouts merely add the 'unmerged-usr'/'unmerged-bin' taint (src/core/taint.c:45-51).

claim_checks.claim: README:333-336 - systemd is regularly tested on amd64, i386, arm64, ppc64el and s390x.
claim_checks.evidence: .github/workflows/unit-tests.yml:24-46 runs the unit-test matrix on x86_64, arm64, armhf (cross), ppc64le and s390x; i386 appears only as a CIFuzz ASan fuzz build (.github/workflows/cifuzz.yml:35-37) and a Packit Copr build target (.packit.yml:37-38); riscv64/armhf are cross-build checks (.github/workflows/build-test.yml:42-47).

claim_checks.claim: README.md:37 (repeated at README:486-488) - stable branches with backported patches are available in the systemd-stable repo.
claim_checks.evidence: Code/docs differ: docs/RELEASE.md:41 says since v256 the stable branches live in systemd/systemd and only older ones are in systemd-stable; CI here triggers on v[0-9]+-stable branches (.github/workflows/unit-tests.yml:8-10) and make-release.yml:15 handles both repositories.

claim_checks.claim: docs/OPTIMIZATIONS.md:64-65 (not README) - 'Timer units currently have no support for calendar times'.
claim_checks.evidence: OnCalendar= is documented (man/systemd.timer.xml:190-225) and implemented (src/core/timer.c:394-451, calendar_spec_next_usec in src/shared/calendarspec.c); shipped timers use it (units/systemd-sysupdate-update.timer:25, units/systemd-sysupdate-reboot.timer:16).

claim_checks.claim: NEWS:3168-3176 (v258; not README) - slice ConcurrencySoftMax=/ConcurrencyHardMax= 'introduces a powerful job execution mechanism ... with support for hierarchial job pools'.
claim_checks.evidence: Limits exist and are hierarchical: soft limit keeps start jobs queued (src/core/unit.c:2035-2036), hard limit fails them with JOB_CONCURRENCY (src/core/unit.c:2030-2031; src/core/job.c:988-989), parent slices are consulted (src/core/slice.c:433-471); v262 adds ActivatingConcurrencyMax= (man/systemd.slice.xml:144-181). Scope is limited to unit activation: jobs live in memory (serialized to a sealed memfd only for re-exec, src/shared/serialize.c:586-614), and no persisted run table or UI was found.

benchmarks.what: Userspace boot time, project self-reported 'if configured properly'; the linked example bootchart is dated 2012-05-12 by its file name (linked SVG not opened); no method or hardware details; unrelated to timers or supervision. No scheduling, timer or supervision measurements are published in the repository.
benchmarks.value: < 1 s for the Core OS (userspace only); < 2 s for a complete up-to-date desktop on simpler modern SSD laptops

risks: Scope: the repository contains no workflow/DAG-run engine, run-history store or scheduler UI. Job and unit state is in memory (serialized to a sealed memfd only for re-exec: src/shared/serialize.c:586-614, src/core/main.c:1334-1346); list-jobs shows only jobs in progress (man/systemctl.xml:1362-1366); systemd-analyze plot covers only the most recent per-unit timing data (man/systemd-analyze.xml:412-417); history is whatever journald retains (Storage= default is fixed at build time via -Djournal-storage-default, meson_options.txt:149-150, man/journald.conf.xml:75-95; size/age limits and vacuuming delete archived files, man/journald.conf.xml:283-318,343-348).

Cancellation/timeout semantics need care: 'systemctl cancel'/CancelJob has no effect on jobs already executing (man/org.freedesktop.systemd1.xml:1498-1501,12801-12804); JobTimeoutSec= cancels the job but leaves the unit running (man/systemd.unit.xml:1173-1190; src/core/job.c:1130-1139); RuntimeMaxSec= has no effect on Type=oneshot (src/core/service.c:1077-1078) and the oneshot start timeout is infinity by default (src/core/service.c:1225-1227), so bounding a hung oneshot command needs an explicit TimeoutStartSec=; Restart=always/on-success are refused for oneshot (src/core/service.c:1059-1060).

Trigger/ordering semantics: a timer firing while its unit is active or still starting is a no-op, no second instance is spawned (man/systemd.timer.xml:50-52; src/core/service.c:6388-6389), and RemainAfterExit=yes services are unsuitable for repeating timers (man/systemd.timer.xml:50-56); start-rate limiting also applies to manual and timer starts (man/systemd.unit.xml:1232-1245) and can fail a unit with start-limit-hit (src/core/service.c:6392-6395); ordering cycles are resolved by deleting a non-anchor job (logged) instead of rejecting the transaction, and only fail with 'Transaction order is cyclic' if no job can be deleted (src/core/transaction.c:487-521); no rollback/compensation feature for side effects was found, only user-written ExecStopPost= cleanup (man/systemd.service.xml:594-598); transient timers created by systemd-run live under /run/systemd/transient (man/systemd.unit.xml:403-404).

Platform: Linux only, non-Linux ports are not accepted (docs/PORTABILITY_AND_STABILITY.md:111-113); PID 1 refuses to run on a cgroup v1 hierarchy (src/core/main.c:3807-3822); kernel >= 5.10 required and >= 5.14 recommended (README:58-68); /usr prefix and merged-/usr expected (README:311-316; src/core/taint.c:45-51); mixing systemd component versions is untested and unsupported upstream (README:383-388); jobs for non-root users that must run while logged out need a lingering user manager (man/loginctl.xml:186-195).

Compatibility churn and experimental parts: v262 changed StartLimitIntervalSec= and other manager rate-limit timers to CLOCK_BOOTTIME (NEWS:121-127), changed UnsetEnvironment= expansion order (NEWS:104-110) and made notify-reload stricter (NEWS:45-50); experimental components may change (systemd-report, man/systemd-report.xml:36-37; systemd-sysupdate marked experimental again, NEWS:135-138; sysupdated D-Bus API removal planned for v263, NEWS:20-24). The set of unit states and internal sockets are declared unstable (docs/PORTABILITY_AND_STABILITY.md:86-98) while the unit-file format, CLI, D-Bus and Varlink interfaces are declared stable (same file:30-49). Feature PRs are held back around -rc tags (.github/development-freeze.yml:7-13).

Documentation drift (code preferred over docs): README:457-469 lists taint flags cgroups-missing/cgroupsv1 that src/core/taint.c no longer sets; README.md:37 and README:486-488 point to systemd-stable although docs/RELEASE.md:41 says stable branches live in this repo since v256; docs/OPTIMIZATIONS.md:64-65 says timers lack calendar support (contradicted by man/systemd.timer.xml:190-225); docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:76 cites src/core/bpf/, which has no files in this tree (BPF sources are under src/bpf/).

Release/supply chain: releases are signed git tags (docs/RELEASE.md:21,43) and a draft GitHub release without attached artifacts, checksums or attestations (.github/workflows/make-release.yml:22-26); no release signing, SBOM or provenance step was found in .github/; binary packages come from OBS and distributions (README.md:41-42). CI pins most actions by commit SHA, but cifuzz.yml uses google/oss-fuzz/...@master (lines 44,55) and cflite-pr.yml uses google/clusterfuzzlite@v1 (line 28).

Licensing and security process: licenses are mixed - LGPL-2.1-or-later for most code, but udev programs are effectively GPL-2.0-or-later, kernel UAPI headers are GPL-2.0 WITH Linux-syscall-note, and some files are MIT/CC0/public domain (LICENSES/README.md:15-82), so README:29 'LGPL-2.1-or-later for all code' is a simplification. Security reports need a real-world end-to-end reproducer on main and maintainers (mostly volunteers) give no fix timeline (docs/SECURITY.md:22-29). Optional network-facing pieces use weaker transport by default when enabled: journal-gatewayd serves plain HTTP unless --cert/--key is given (man/systemd-journal-gatewayd.service.xml:38-42; preset-disabled at presets/90-systemd.preset:68-70) and experimental 'systemd-report upload' accepts http:// and --trust=all (man/systemd-report.xml:134-143,170-174).

checks.statement: Build from source with Meson/Ninja, then install: meson setup build/ && ninja -C build/ ; sudo meson install -C build/ --no-rebuild (or: DESTDIR=... meson install -C build/)
checks.note: README:282-283 'To build in directory build/: meson setup build/ && ninja -C build/'; README:292-296 'Useful commands' include 'sudo meson install -C build/ --no-rebuild' and 'DESTDIR=... meson install -C build/'. Commands match verbatim. Checked at commit 8cc40e0 (meson.version = 262).

LICENSE.LGPL2.1:1-2 is the GNU Lesser General Public License v2.1 text; README:29 'LGPL-2.1-or-later for all code, exceptions noted in LICENSES/README.md'; LICENSES/README.md:15-17 names LGPL-2.1-or-later as the main license. Exceptions are real but disclosed in the dossier's risks: udev programs effectively GPL-2.0-or-later (LICENSES/README.md:22-23,32-34; LICENSE.GPL2 also present), kernel uapi headers GPL-2.0 WITH Linux-syscall-note, a few MIT/MIT-0/CC0/BSD/public-domain files (lines 37-81). About 168 of the files under src/ carry non-LGPL-2.1-or-later SPDX headers, all in those exception groups.

checks.statement: yes - amd64 regularly tested (README:333-336); unit tests on x86_64 ubuntu-24.04 runners (.github/workflows/unit-tests.yml:24-27); requires Linux >= 5.10 (>= 5.14 recommended; README:58-68), cgroup v2 (src/core/main.c:3807-3822), glibc >= 2.34 or musl >= 1.2.6 (README:213-214), merged /usr (README:311-316)
checks.note: README:334 lists 'amd64, i386, arm64, ppc64el, and s390x'. unit-tests.yml:24 sets 'runner: [ ubuntu-24.04 ]' for all six run phases. The file never says x86_64; that is inferred from GitHub's plain ubuntu-24.04 label, while the other arches use the -arm/-ppc64le/-s390x labels at lines 29-36. README:58 says kernels below 5.10 are 'not supported at all'; README:65-67 calls 5.14 the 'recommended baseline' and mentions the 'old-kernel' taint. main.c:3807-3822 refuses to run on a cgroup v1 hierarchy. README:213-214 gives glibc >= 2.34 and musl >= 1.2.6. README:311-314 says the prefix must be /usr/ and split-usr/unmerged-usr systems are no longer supported. The 5.10 floor is stated in README only and not enforced in code, as the dossier's own claim_checks already says.

checks.statement: yes - systemctl (list-timers, list-jobs, cancel, kill, clean, freeze), systemd-run and its run0 symlink (transient timers via --on-calendar/--on-active; --wait propagates the unit result as exit status), journalctl (-I/--invocation), systemd-analyze (calendar, verify, dot, plot), loginctl enable-linger; CLI declared stable but its human-readable output generally not
checks.citation: src/systemctl/meson.build:43-56; src/systemctl/systemctl.c:922,957-963,1022-1024; src/run/meson.build:3-13; man/systemd-run.xml:453-506; src/run/run.c:2491-2502; src/journal/journalctl.c:1139; man/journalctl.xml:354-376; src/analyze/analyze.c:216-273; man/loginctl.xml:186-195; docs/PORTABILITY_AND_STABILITY.md:42-49
checks.note: All ten citations match. systemctl.c: list-timers at 922, kill 957, clean 959, freeze 961, list-jobs 1022, cancel 1024. run/meson.build:3-13 builds systemd-run and install_symlink('run0'). systemd-run.xml:453-506 documents --on-active/--on-boot/--on-startup/--on-unit-*/--on-calendar/--on-clock-change/--timer-property. run.c:2491-2502 maps the result (success/exit-code/signal) to the exit status, inside the 'if (arg_wait || arg_stdio != ARG_STDIO_NONE)' branch opened at 2449. journalctl.c:1139 is DEFINE_MAIN_FUNCTION(run); journalctl.xml:354-376 documents -I/--invocation. analyze.c has plot at 220, dot 222, calendar 262, verify 270. loginctl.xml:186-195 documents enable-linger. PORTABILITY_AND_STABILITY.md:42-49 declares the CLI stable but its output generally not stable.

checks.statement: man/systemd.timer.xml:50-52 - if the unit to activate is already active when a timer elapses it is not restarted and no new instance is spawned (verified: yes)
checks.note: systemd.timer.xml:50-51: 'already active at the time the timer elapses it is not restarted, but simply left running. There is no concept of spawning new service instances'. timer.c:668 calls manager_add_job(..., JOB_START, trigger, JOB_REPLACE, ...). unit.c:1960-1962 returns -EALREADY for active/reloading units, and job.c:970-971 finishes that job as JOB_DONE. service.c:6388-6389 returns false for SERVICE_CONDITION/START_PRE/START/START_POST before unit_test_start_limit() is reached; unit.c:2012-2015 then returns without calling ->start. So there is no second run and no start-limit increment, as the evidence says.
